category: Image Processing Toolbox > Segmentation, Analysis & Transforms
description: Thresholding and segmentation algorithms, connected-component labelling and region measurement, shape detection, and image transforms such as the DCT, Radon and Hough transforms.

tools.name: imbinarize
tools.description: Convert a grayscale image to binary by global or locally adaptive thresholding. The global method uses Otsu's criterion by default, while the adaptive method computes a threshold surface that follows uneven illumination. This is the standard entry point for binarization.
tools.usage:
BW = imbinarize(I)
BW = imbinarize(I, method)
BW = imbinarize(I, T)
BW = imbinarize(I, 'adaptive', Name, Value)

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: 'global' (default, Otsu) or 'adaptive'.

parameters.name: T
parameters.description: An explicit threshold, scalar or a per-pixel threshold image.

parameters.name: 'Sensitivity'
parameters.description: 0 to 1 for adaptive thresholding (default 0.5); higher thresholds more pixels as foreground.

parameters.name: 'ForegroundPolarity'
parameters.description: 'bright' (default) or 'dark'.

tools.name: graythresh
tools.description: Compute a global image threshold using Otsu's method, which maximizes the between-class variance of the two resulting pixel groups. It also returns the effectiveness metric, a 0-1 score telling you how bimodal the histogram is. Use the metric to decide whether global thresholding is appropriate at all.
tools.usage:
T = graythresh(I)
[T, EM] = graythresh(I)

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Grayscale image; the returned threshold is normalized to [0, 1].

tools.notes: Multiply T by the class maximum (e.g. 255) if you need an absolute intensity threshold.

tools.name: multithresh
tools.description: Compute multiple global thresholds using multilevel Otsu, partitioning the image into N+1 intensity classes. Pair it with imquantize to produce a labelled multi-level image. Use it when the scene has several distinct intensity populations rather than just foreground and background.
tools.usage:
thresh = multithresh(A)
thresh = multithresh(A, N)
[thresh, metric] = multithresh(___)

parameters.name: N
parameters.description: Number of thresholds (default 1); yields N+1 classes. Values above about 5 get slow.

parameters.name: metric
parameters.description: Effectiveness of the thresholding, 0 to 1.

tools.name: imquantize
tools.description: Quantize an image using a set of thresholds, returning an index image where each pixel gets the number of the interval it falls in. You can supply your own output values so it doubles as an arbitrary piecewise-constant mapping. It is the natural companion to multithresh.
tools.usage:
quant_A = imquantize(A, levels)
quant_A = imquantize(A, levels, values)
[quant_A, index] = imquantize(___)

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: Monotonically increasing vector of threshold values.

parameters.name: values
parameters.description: Optional vector of length numel(levels)+1 giving the output value per interval.

tools.name: bwlabel
tools.description: Label connected components in a 2-D binary image, returning a matrix in which the pixels of the nth object all have value n. The optional second output gives the number of objects found. It is the classic way to count and index discrete objects after thresholding.
tools.usage:
L = bwlabel(BW)
L = bwlabel(BW, conn)
[L, n] = bwlabel(___)

parameters.name: BW
parameters.description: Binary image.

parameters.name: conn
parameters.description: Connectivity, 4 or 8 (default 8).

tools.notes: bwconncomp is faster and more memory-efficient for large images; bwlabeln handles N dimensions.

tools.name: bwconncomp
tools.description: Find connected components in a binary image of any dimension and return them as a structure with a cell array of pixel index lists. It uses much less memory than a full label matrix and is the recommended modern alternative to bwlabel. Its output can be passed directly to regionprops or converted with labelmatrix.
tools.usage:
CC = bwconncomp(BW)
CC = bwconncomp(BW, conn)

parameters.name: BW
parameters.description: Binary image or volume.

parameters.name: conn
parameters.description: Connectivity: 4/8 in 2-D, 6/18/26 in 3-D (default 8 / 26).

tools.name: regionprops
tools.description: Measure geometric and intensity properties of labelled image regions: area, centroid, bounding box, eccentricity, orientation, perimeter, circularity, mean intensity and many more. Request 'table' output to get a ready-to-analyse table. It is the workhorse of quantitative image analysis.
tools.usage:
stats = regionprops(BW, properties)
stats = regionprops(L, properties)
stats = regionprops(CC, I, properties)
stats = regionprops('table', ___)

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: 'Area', 'Centroid', 'BoundingBox', 'MajorAxisLength', 'MinorAxisLength', 'Eccentricity', 'Orientation', 'Perimeter', 'Circularity', 'Solidity', 'Extent', 'EulerNumber', 'MeanIntensity', 'PixelIdxList', 'all', 'basic'.

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Optional grayscale image for intensity measurements.

parameters.name: 'table'
parameters.description: Return a table instead of a struct array.

tools.notes: regionprops3 measures 3-D volumes. Perimeter and Circularity are only meaningful for reasonably large, smooth objects.

tools.name: bwboundaries
tools.description: Trace the exterior boundaries of objects and the boundaries of holes inside them, returning each as an ordered list of [row col] coordinates. The optional label matrix and adjacency matrix outputs describe the parent-child nesting of objects and holes. Use it for contour plotting and shape descriptors.
tools.usage:
B = bwboundaries(BW)
B = bwboundaries(BW, conn, options)
[B, L, n, A] = bwboundaries(___)

parameters.name: conn
parameters.description: Connectivity, 4 or 8 (default 8).

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: 'holes' (default, trace holes too) or 'noholes'.

tools.name: watershed
tools.description: Apply the watershed transform, which treats the image as a topographic surface and finds the ridge lines separating catchment basins. It is the classic method for splitting touching objects. Applied naively it massively over-segments, so it is almost always preceded by imimposemin with well-chosen markers.
tools.usage:
L = watershed(A)
L = watershed(A, conn)

parameters.name: A
parameters.description: Grayscale image or volume, usually a gradient magnitude or a negated distance transform.

parameters.name: conn
parameters.description: Connectivity (default 8 in 2-D, 26 in 3-D).

tools.notes: Watershed ridge pixels are labelled 0. Control over-segmentation with imhmin, imextendedmin or imimposemin.

tools.name: imsegkmeans
tools.description: Segment an image into k clusters using k-means on pixel feature vectors (colour channels, or any multichannel feature stack such as Gabor responses). It returns a label image and optionally the cluster centres so you can classify further images consistently. Works well for colour-based segmentation, especially in L*a*b* space.
tools.usage:
L = imsegkmeans(I, k)
[L, centers] = imsegkmeans(I, k)
L = imsegkmeans(I, centers)
L = imsegkmeans(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Number of clusters.

parameters.name: centers
parameters.description: Precomputed cluster centres to apply to a new image.

parameters.name: 'NumAttempts'
parameters.description: Number of random restarts (default 3).

parameters.name: 'NormalizeInput'
parameters.description: Logical; z-score each channel first (default true).

tools.notes: imsegkmeans3 handles volumes. Input must be single/uint8/uint16, so cast features with single().

tools.name: activecontour
tools.description: Refine an initial segmentation mask by evolving an active contour (snake) using the Chan-Vese or edge-based level-set method. It pulls a rough mask onto the true object boundary using region statistics or edge information. Use it after a crude threshold or a manually drawn ROI.
tools.usage:
bw = activecontour(A, mask)
bw = activecontour(A, mask, n)
bw = activecontour(A, mask, method)
bw = activecontour(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: mask
parameters.description: Initial binary mask; must be entirely inside or entirely outside the object.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Number of iterations (default 100).

parameters.name: method
parameters.description: 'Chan-Vese' (default, region based) or 'edge' (gradient based).

parameters.name: 'SmoothFactor'
parameters.description: Boundary regularity; higher gives smoother contours.

parameters.name: 'ContractionBias'
parameters.description: Positive contracts the contour, negative expands it.

tools.name: superpixels
tools.description: Over-segment an image into compact, perceptually uniform superpixel regions using the SLIC algorithm. Superpixels reduce thousands of pixels to a few hundred regions that respect object boundaries, which speeds up downstream segmentation and classification enormously. Returns a label matrix and the number of superpixels actually produced.
tools.usage:
[L, N] = superpixels(A, N)
[L, N] = superpixels(A, N, Name, Value)

parameters.name: N
parameters.description: Requested number of superpixels; the actual count may differ slightly.

parameters.name: 'Compactness'
parameters.description: Higher values give more regular, square-ish superpixels (default 10 for RGB).

parameters.name: 'Method'
parameters.description: 'slic0' (default, adaptive compactness) or 'slic'.

parameters.name: 'NumIterations'
parameters.description: Refinement iterations (default 10).

tools.notes: superpixels3 works on volumes. Use label2idx to get pixel index lists per superpixel for feature averaging.

tools.name: grabcut
tools.description: Segment an image into foreground and background using the GrabCut graph-cut algorithm, seeded by a bounding ROI and optional scribbles. It works on superpixel labels rather than raw pixels, which makes it fast. Use it for interactive object cutout with very little user input.
tools.usage:
BW = grabcut(A, L, ROI)
BW = grabcut(A, L, ROI, foreind, backind)
BW = grabcut(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: L
parameters.description: Superpixel label matrix, typically from superpixels.

parameters.name: ROI
parameters.description: Binary mask or [x y w h] rectangle enclosing the object.

parameters.name: foreind, backind
parameters.description: Indices of superpixels known to be foreground/background.

parameters.name: 'Connectivity'
parameters.description: 4 or 8 (default 8).

tools.notes: lazysnapping is the related interactive graph-cut function driven purely by scribbles.

tools.name: imfindcircles
tools.description: Detect circular objects using a circular Hough transform, returning centres, radii and a per-circle metric strength. You supply a radius range and optionally the polarity of the objects against the background. It is remarkably robust to partial occlusion and overlap.
tools.usage:
centers = imfindcircles(A, radius)
[centers, radii] = imfindcircles(A, radiusRange)
[centers, radii, metric] = imfindcircles(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: radiusRange
parameters.description: [rmin rmax] in pixels; keep the ratio below about 3 for good results.

parameters.name: 'ObjectPolarity'
parameters.description: 'bright' (default) or 'dark' objects relative to the background.

parameters.name: 'Sensitivity'
parameters.description: 0 to 1 (default 0.85); higher finds more circles including weak ones.

parameters.name: 'EdgeThreshold'
parameters.description: 0 to 1 gradient threshold for edge pixels.

parameters.name: 'Method'
parameters.description: 'PhaseCode' (default) or 'TwoStage'.

tools.notes: Use viscircles to draw the result. Very small radii (below about 5 px) are unreliable.

tools.name: viscircles
tools.description: Draw circles of given centres and radii on the current axes, typically to visualize imfindcircles output. Colour, line style and width are configurable. Returns a handle group so the circles can be deleted or restyled later.
tools.usage:
viscircles(centers, radii)
viscircles(ax, centers, radii)
h = viscircles(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: centers
parameters.description: n-by-2 matrix of [x y] centre coordinates.

parameters.name: radii
parameters.description: Vector of radii.

parameters.name: 'Color'
parameters.description: Circle colour, default 'red'.

parameters.name: 'LineWidth'
parameters.description: Line width in points.

tools.name: hough
tools.description: Compute the standard Hough transform of a binary image, producing a parameter-space accumulator indexed by angle theta and distance rho. Peaks in this accumulator correspond to straight lines in the image. Use it as the first step of line detection, followed by houghpeaks and houghlines.
tools.usage:
[H, theta, rho] = hough(BW)
[H, theta, rho] = hough(BW, Name, Value)

parameters.name: BW
parameters.description: Binary image, typically an edge map from edge().

parameters.name: 'Theta'
parameters.description: Vector of angles in degrees to search, default -90:89.

parameters.name: 'RhoResolution'
parameters.description: Spacing of the rho axis in pixels (default 1).

tools.name: houghpeaks
tools.description: Find the strongest peaks in a Hough transform accumulator, suppressing a neighbourhood around each peak so nearby duplicates are not returned. It returns row/column indices into H that identify candidate lines. The threshold and NHoodSize options control how many and how distinct the peaks are.
tools.usage:
peaks = houghpeaks(H, numpeaks)
peaks = houghpeaks(H, numpeaks, Name, Value)

parameters.name: numpeaks
parameters.description: Maximum number of peaks to identify (default 1).

parameters.name: 'Threshold'
parameters.description: Minimum accumulator value to be considered a peak (default 0.5*max(H(:))).

parameters.name: 'NHoodSize'
parameters.description: [m n] odd-sized neighbourhood suppressed around each found peak.

tools.name: houghlines
tools.description: Extract actual line segments from an image given Hough peaks, returning their endpoints, theta and rho. It walks along each candidate line, merging collinear pixels separated by less than FillGap and discarding segments shorter than MinLength. This turns a parametric peak into a concrete, drawable segment.
tools.usage:
lines = houghlines(BW, theta, rho, peaks)
lines = houghlines(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: theta, rho
parameters.description: Axis vectors returned by hough.

parameters.name: peaks
parameters.description: Peak indices from houghpeaks.

parameters.name: 'FillGap'
parameters.description: Maximum gap in pixels to bridge between collinear segments (default 20).

parameters.name: 'MinLength'
parameters.description: Discard segments shorter than this (default 40).

tools.name: radon
tools.description: Compute the Radon transform, the set of line integrals of an image taken at specified projection angles. It is the mathematical model of a CT sinogram and also a robust way to detect dominant orientations. iradon performs filtered back-projection to reconstruct the image.
tools.usage:
R = radon(I)
R = radon(I, theta)
[R, xp] = radon(___)

parameters.name: theta
parameters.description: Vector of projection angles in degrees (default 0:179).

parameters.name: xp
parameters.description: Output coordinate vector along the projection axis.

tools.name: iradon
tools.description: Reconstruct an image from its Radon transform (projections) using filtered back-projection. The filter choice trades spatial resolution against noise amplification, and the frequency scaling parameter provides additional smoothing. This is the standard analytic CT reconstruction routine.
tools.usage:
I = iradon(R, theta)
I = iradon(R, theta, interp, filter, frequency_scaling, output_size)
[I, H] = iradon(___)

parameters.name: theta
parameters.description: Projection angles matching those used by radon.

parameters.name: interp
parameters.description: 'linear' (default), 'nearest', 'spline', 'pchip', 'cubic'.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: 'Ram-Lak' (default), 'Shepp-Logan', 'Cosine', 'Hamming', 'Hann', or 'none'.

parameters.name: frequency_scaling
parameters.description: 0 to 1; values below 1 lowpass the filter to reduce noise.

parameters.name: output_size
parameters.description: Number of rows and columns in the reconstruction.

tools.name: dct2
tools.description: Compute the two-dimensional discrete cosine transform of an image. The DCT concentrates most of the signal energy into a few low-frequency coefficients, which is why it underpins JPEG compression. Use it for compression experiments, watermarking and frequency-domain filtering of real images.
tools.usage:
B = dct2(A)
B = dct2(A, m, n)
B = dct2(A, [m n])

parameters.name: A
parameters.description: Input image (converted to double internally).

parameters.name: m, n
parameters.description: Output size; the input is zero-padded or cropped to this size.

tools.notes: For block-based JPEG-style processing combine blockproc with dct2 on 8-by-8 blocks.

tools.name: idct2
tools.description: Compute the inverse 2-D discrete cosine transform, recovering an image from its DCT coefficients. Zeroing small coefficients before calling it demonstrates lossy compression directly. Output size can be forced with the m and n arguments.
tools.usage:
B = idct2(A)
B = idct2(A, m, n)
B = idct2(A, [m n])

parameters.name: A
parameters.description: Matrix of DCT coefficients.

parameters.name: m, n
parameters.description: Size of the reconstructed output.

tools.name: blockproc
tools.description: Apply a function to each distinct or overlapping block of an image, assembling the results into an output image. It can stream very large images from and to files without loading them into memory. Use it for block-based transforms, tiled statistics and processing images larger than RAM.
tools.usage:
B = blockproc(A, [m n], fun)
blockproc(src_filename, [m n], fun, 'Destination', dest)
B = blockproc(___, Name, Value)

parameters.name: [m n]
parameters.description: Block size in pixels.

parameters.name: fun
parameters.description: Function handle taking a block struct with fields .data, .blockSize, .location.

parameters.name: 'BorderSize'
parameters.description: [v h] extra pixels added around each block for context.

parameters.name: 'UseParallel'
parameters.description: Logical; distribute blocks across a parallel pool.

parameters.name: 'Destination'
parameters.description: Output filename for file-to-file streaming.

tools.name: boundarymask
tools.description: Create a binary mask marking the boundaries between labelled regions or the outline of a binary mask. It is the standard way to draw superpixel or segmentation borders on top of an image. Connectivity determines whether boundaries are 4- or 8-connected.
tools.usage:
mask = boundarymask(L)
mask = boundarymask(BW)
mask = boundarymask(___, conn)

parameters.name: L / BW
parameters.description: Label matrix or binary mask.

parameters.name: conn
parameters.description: Connectivity, 4 or 8 (default 8).

tools.name: label2rgb
tools.description: Convert a label matrix into a colour image by assigning a distinct colour to each label. The background label (0 by default) can be given its own colour and the colour order can be shuffled so adjacent regions differ. It is the standard way to display segmentation results.
tools.usage:
RGB = label2rgb(L)
RGB = label2rgb(L, cmap)
RGB = label2rgb(L, cmap, zerocolor)
RGB = label2rgb(L, cmap, zerocolor, order)

parameters.name: cmap
parameters.description: Colormap name, function handle or n-by-3 matrix (default 'jet').

parameters.name: zerocolor
parameters.description: RGB triple or colour name for label 0 (default [1 1 1]).

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: 'noshuffle' (default) or 'shuffle'.

tools.name: bwselect
tools.description: Select individual objects in a binary image by supplying seed points, either programmatically or by clicking. Every connected component containing a seed is returned; everything else is discarded. Use it to isolate specific objects after labelling.
tools.usage:
BW2 = bwselect(BW, c, r)
BW2 = bwselect(BW, c, r, n)
[BW2, idx] = bwselect(___)
BW2 = bwselect(BW)

parameters.name: c, r
parameters.description: Column and row coordinates of the seed points.

parameters.name: n
parameters.description: Connectivity, 4 or 8 (default 8).

tools.name: bwpropfilt
tools.description: Keep only the binary objects whose value of a chosen regionprops property falls in a range, or the n extreme objects by that property. It generalizes bwareafilt to any shape measure such as eccentricity, solidity or perimeter. Very useful for rejecting objects that are the right size but the wrong shape.
tools.usage:
BW2 = bwpropfilt(BW, attrib, range)
BW2 = bwpropfilt(BW, attrib, n)
BW2 = bwpropfilt(BW, I, attrib, ___)
BW2 = bwpropfilt(___, keep)

parameters.name: attrib
parameters.description: Any regionprops scalar property name, e.g. 'Eccentricity', 'Solidity', 'Perimeter', 'MeanIntensity'.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: [min max] acceptable values.

parameters.name: n / keep
parameters.description: Number of objects and whether to keep the 'largest' or 'smallest'.

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Grayscale image, required for intensity-based attributes.

tools.name: imoverlay
tools.description: Burn a binary mask into an image as a solid colour, producing an RGB result. Unlike labeloverlay it is fully opaque and takes a single mask rather than a label matrix. Use it to mark detected boundaries or regions for a figure or report.
tools.usage:
B = imoverlay(A, BW)
B = imoverlay(A, BW, color)

parameters.name: A
parameters.description: Grayscale or RGB base image.

parameters.name: BW
parameters.description: Binary mask the same size as A.

parameters.name: color
parameters.description: Colour name or RGB triplet, default 'yellow'.

tools.name: roipoly
tools.description: Define a polygonal region of interest and return it as a binary mask, either interactively by clicking vertices or programmatically from coordinate vectors. The mask can then be used to restrict any analysis to that region. It is the simplest way to script a non-rectangular ROI.
tools.usage:
BW = roipoly(I, xi, yi)
BW = roipoly(xi, yi)
[BW, xi, yi] = roipoly(I)
BW = roipoly(x, y, I, xi, yi)

parameters.name: I
parameters.description: Image used for sizing and (interactively) for display.

parameters.name: xi, yi
parameters.description: Polygon vertex coordinates.

tools.notes: poly2mask does the same conversion without needing an image. drawpolygon gives modern interactive ROI objects.

tools.name: poly2mask
tools.description: Convert polygon vertex coordinates directly into a binary mask of a given size, with proper anti-aliased edge decisions. Unlike roipoly it needs no image and no display, which makes it ideal for batch processing and for converting annotation files into masks. Multiple polygons can be combined by logical OR.
tools.usage: BW = poly2mask(xi, yi, m, n)

parameters.name: xi, yi
parameters.description: Polygon vertex x and y coordinates.

parameters.name: m, n
parameters.description: Number of rows and columns in the output mask.
